questions.q: In StaleLeadCleanupBatch, what is Database.Stateful used for?
options: To allow the batch class to make HTTP callouts
To carry leadsArchived and leadsFailed across every chunk, so finish reports an accurate org-wide total rather than just the last chunk's numbers
To increase the default chunk size from 200 to 2,000
To let the start method return an Iterable instead of a QueryLocator
questions.explain: Database.Stateful preserves leadsArchived and leadsFailed as instance variables across every chunk's transaction, letting finish report the true running totals instead of whatever only the final chunk happened to see.

questions.q: Why does the lab use Database.update(toUpdate, false) instead of a plain update toUpdate; statement?
options: Database.update(list, false) deletes the records instead of updating them
The false argument disables all validation rules for the DML operation
There's no actual difference between the two syntaxes
Passing false as the second argument allows partial success — some records in the list succeed even if others in the same chunk fail, instead of the whole DML operation rolling back
questions.explain: Database.update(list, false) sets 'all or nothing' to false, allowing partial success: some Leads in the chunk can succeed while others fail, rather than one bad record rolling back the entire chunk's DML.

questions.q: Why does the batch class's start method filter for IsConverted = false and the date/activity conditions directly in SOQL, rather than filtering inside execute?
options: SOQL filtering in start is required syntax and cannot be done any other way
Filtering inside execute is not technically possible in Batch Apex
Doing the real record-selection logic in start's query keeps execute's per-chunk logic simple, since execute only ever sees Leads that already qualify
It has no effect on the design — the filters could be placed anywhere with identical results
questions.explain: Doing the filtering in start's SOQL query means execute's per-record work stays simple and focused, since every record passed into execute has already been confirmed to match the cleanup criteria.

questions.q: After running Database.executeBatch(new StaleLeadCleanupBatch(), 200), which query from this lesson checks the job's progress and error count?
options: SELECT Id FROM Lead WHERE Archived__c = true LIMIT 1
SELECT Status, NumberOfErrors, TotalJobItems, JobItemsProcessed FROM AsyncApexJob WHERE Id = :jobId
SELECT CronExpression FROM CronTrigger WHERE Id = :jobId
SELECT COUNT(Id) FROM AsyncApexJob
questions.explain: Querying AsyncApexJob by the job Id returned from Database.executeBatch, selecting Status, NumberOfErrors, TotalJobItems, and JobItemsProcessed, is the monitoring technique from Lesson 9 used here to verify the job's progress and outcome.

questions.q: The lesson keeps the batch's chunk size at the default of 200. Why is that a reasonable choice for this specific job?
options: 200 is the only legal chunk size Batch Apex supports
A larger chunk size would be illegal for a QueryLocator-based start method
Because Database.Stateful requires exactly 200 records per chunk
Each record's per-chunk work is lightweight — setting two fields and one DML update, with no callouts or nested per-record queries — so there's no reason to shrink the chunk size
questions.explain: A smaller chunk size is worth considering when per-record work inside execute is heavy (multiple callouts, nested queries). Here, each record's work is lightweight, so the default 200 is a reasonable, uncomplicated choice.
